overview: Cohort study of patients with type 2 diabetes due for kidney testing across 31 practices, using the staggered rollout of dashboard version 2 (16 practices from March 2026, 15 from September 2026) as a concurrent comparison.
population: All patients with type 2 diabetes registered on 2 March 2026 who are due or become due for kidney testing before 6 September 2026 (about 4,900 of 9,870).
exposure: Registration with a practice on dashboard version 2 during the window; feature use from usage logs.
procedures: Pseudonymised extracts under DSA-PCN-2025-07 give due dates, test results and hospital results where linked; usage logs give list views, chart views and log-ins per practice. Pre-rollout trends from 2024 and 2025 are compared between waves before outcome data for 2026 are examined.

outcomes.name: Both kidney tests completed
outcomes.measure: eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio both resulted within the window, among patients due
outcomes.why: The guideline's aim; completed tests, not orders (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Urine albumin test completed
outcomes.why: The test most often not completed.

outcomes.name: Duplicate kidney testing
outcomes.measure: Kidney test in primary care within 30 days of a hospital result

outcomes.name: Patient list use
outcomes.measure: Practice-level list views per month from usage logs
outcomes.why: Shows whether the feature expected to act was used (claim c4).

feasibility: Extracts and logs exist; the analysis fits within the lead's time over three months after September 2026.
biasMitigation: Pre-rollout trends compared between waves before outcomes are examined
Outcome from laboratory results, not orders

biasFlags.label: Schedule related to performance
biasFlags.note: Checked with pre-rollout trends; defeating criterion k3 stays unknown until then.

biasFlags.label: Spillover between practices sharing staff
biasFlags.note: Shared staff are identified and a sensitivity analysis excludes those practices.

flags: Three adjustment variables fixed in advance
parsimony.simplestPath: One exposure, one primary outcome, one mixed model with baseline adjustment.

theoreticalFramework: Clinical Performance Feedback Intervention Theory is used only to name the feedback features being compared.
summary: Cohort across a staggered rollout with completed tests as the primary outcome and duplicate testing as the balancing measure.
